blocks.heading: Scope of the Review Gate
blocks.text: This section owns the release decision for the candidate AANEC-relaxed trapped-surface theorem. The formal reasoning plan remains unverified: the Misner-Sharp compactness parameter and the explicit averaged null-convergence condition lack closed mathematical forms, so the derivation cannot be audited as a proof. Separately, the astrophysical mass-gap application is confounded by explosion energetics, fallback, equation-of-state physics, rotation, magnetic fields, nonspherical dynamics, and binary evolution. These two limitations must remain separate: neither the formal gap nor the empirical confounding constitutes a completed counterexample or an observed failure. The review gate therefore asks whether the dependency ledger can be closed before the theorem status is allowed to update.

blocks.heading: Limitation and Review Decision Matrix
blocks.text:
| Decision item | Limitation or review requirement | Evidence or design basis | Release condition | Allowed conclusion |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Formal reasoning plan | The canonical plan status requires qualified human review before any theorem-level claim is released. | Survey synthesis notes that pointwise energy conditions are systematically violated by quantum fields, motivating averaged or inequality-based replacements; AANEC alone does not automatically deliver the local or integrated focusing used in Penrose-type arguments. | A reviewer confirms the domain of admissible metrics, the AANEC statement, and the independent averaged-focusing hypothesis. | The theorem may be presented as a scoped conjecture, not as a proved result. |
| Compactness definition | The Misner-Sharp compactness parameter has no supplied formula, so thresholds cannot be computed. | The derivation step that converts negative null expansions into a trapped surface depends on this symbol; the threshold argument therefore has an open dependency. | A reviewer supplies the effective-mass formula and the threshold convention for the chosen metric class. | The compactness-bound lemma remains candidate; no numeric mass gap is inferred. |
| Averaged-focusing obligation | The explicit averaged null-convergence condition is stated but not formalized, so proof obligations cannot be checked. | Candidate witnesses evade trapped surfaces while assuming AANEC; whether they satisfy the additional focusing hypothesis is indeterminate. | A reviewer writes the integral or inequality that distinguishes the added condition from AANEC and applies it to the witnesses. | Falsifier search stays unverified; the branch is no-information, not proof of failure. |
| Astrophysical relevance | The observed 2-5 solar mass gap is not a direct consequence of the formal theorem. | Population and stellar-evolution evidence attributes gap structure to explosion mechanisms, fallback, pair-instability processes, metallicity, and binary channels; gravitational-wave catalogs report gap-region candidates that challenge simple thresholds. | The manuscript separates the formal conjecture from the astrophysical consistency discussion and names the confounders. | The mass gap is treated as a constraint, not as theorem-derived prediction. |
| No-information branches | Missing definitions and unresolved proof obligations trigger no-information branches rather than a theorem failure. | The audit registry withholds theorem-status updates when the dependency is unavailable. | The missing symbol or obligation is resolved, or the scope is narrowed to exclude it. | The plan remains valid as a proposal; no conclusion of invalidity is warranted. |

blocks.heading: Concrete Release and Escalation Protocol
blocks.text: Before escalation, a qualified reviewer must (1) confirm that the formal claim is labeled candidate or unverified and that no observed result is implied; (2) supply or formally exclude the compactness definition and the averaged-focusing inequality, recording the choice in the definition ledger; (3) verify that each proposed counterexample is checked against every stated assumption, so that a witness failing the added focusing condition is classified as a scope delimiter rather than a falsifier; and (4) ensure the mass-gap discussion cites the confounder list and does not present the theorem as an explanation of the observed gap. If any condition is unmet, the route is released only as a scoped conjecture with the no-information branches visible. The next stage should consume this gate as a precondition: derivation work proceeds only on metrics and hypotheses that survive the review, and any released theorem statement must carry the restricted model class explicitly.

claim_provenance.statement: The formal reasoning plan is a scoped conjecture: the compactness parameter and the explicit averaged null-convergence condition lack closed forms, so the derivation cannot be audited as a completed proof.

The observed stellar mass gap is governed by supernova explosion energetics, fallback, equation-of-state physics, rotation, magnetic fields, nonspherical dynamics, and binary evolution, so the formal theorem does not by itself explain the gap.
A qualified reviewer must confirm the admissible metric class, the AANEC statement, and the independent averaged-focusing hypothesis before any theorem-level claim is released.
The compactness definition and the averaged-focusing proof obligation must be supplied or formally excluded so that candidate witnesses can be classified as scope delimiters or genuine falsifiers.
No-information branches withhold theorem-status updates when a dependency is unavailable; they are neither proof of failure nor a reason to describe the research plan as invalid.
Release requires the reviewer to verify claim separation, assumption-by-assumption counterexample checks, and an explicit restricted model class in any theorem statement.
Formal and empirical claims must remain separate: the mass gap is treated as an astrophysical consistency constraint, not as a theorem-derived prediction.

review_items.text: The final canonical formal_reasoning_plan status requires qualified human review; release is gated on confirming the admissible model class, the AANEC statement, and the independent averaged-focusing hypothesis.
